purpose: THE LOGPROB-AS-JUDGE PROBE. One arm, one contact per sample, no knowledge, no mechanism: the sealed closed-list direct comparator's configuration with ONE key added -- decoding_params.logprobs true / top_logprobs 5 -- so the frozen core's own per-token distribution is recorded beside every answer instead of being discarded. It measures whether that confidence predicts the core's own errors well enough to serve as a Reviewer signal (docs/readiness/2026-09-08-agent-system-episode-and-core-pressure-v1.md names 'decode-confidence signals from the sealed trace' as a judge that is named but not built). It is NOT a mechanism cell: no evidence, no retrieval, no second contact, no post-processor, and it makes no claim about SLURP accuracy. Owner directive 2026-09-08: analyse logprobs first; the proposal needs experimental evidence.
one_key_basis: The baseline fragment is the comparator's OWN fragment, reused byte for byte -- not a sibling -- so the arm, the policy, the evidence source, the instruction template and fill, the packet promotion receipt and its sha256, the representation and matcher ids and the declared scorers are literally the same file. The dataset fragment is the comparator's own. The model fragment is the comparator's own model fragment plus exactly two decoding_params keys: logprobs true and top_logprobs 5. Everything else in it -- model_lock_key, materialization root, transport, base_url, timeout, runtime receipt, all fifteen server_args, temperature 0, seed 20260803, max_tokens 64, id_slot per-sample, prompt_order speech-query-prefix-v2, profile_slot_count 8, speech_feature_root and both server_env entries -- is byte-identical. The wire check scripts/slurp_logprob_wire_check.py proves the payload-binding stage and the HTTP request body differ by exactly those two keys and nothing else.
profile_basis: bounded-discovery-probe, not baseline-reproduction. This cell does not reproduce a published protocol and its outputs are not a comparator: it adds a decoding parameter that the sealed comparator did not carry, and greedy decoding is not bitwise reproducible across batch compositions on llama-server, so its answers are a NEW arm's answers. Every relation the read measures is therefore measured WITHIN this arm -- its own official scores against its own confidences -- and never against the sealed comparator's rows.
declared_protocol_change: decoding_params.logprobs / top_logprobs are declared in the model fragment, hashed into config_hash by core.config.compose like every other top-level key, and therefore move protocol_hash. They are a decoding parameter, exactly like temperature and seed; they are NOT added to the arm's D2-frozen visible field set (e0.d2_leakage.ARM_VISIBLE_FIELDS is unchanged) and no new request field is introduced. On the wire they are the OpenAI-compatible chat keys the pinned llama-server maps to its native n_probs (llama.cpp-featcache 04ccc72a, tools/server/server-common.cpp:1525-1529).
budget_basis: 1,000 contacts, one per sample, plus margin for the harness's own accounting and one permitted recovery smoke = 1,050 planned model calls, matching the comparator's own cell. Metered speech is the roster's own 2,884.7936875 seconds rounded up to 3,000. GPU hours 0.5 against a comparator that flew the same 1,000 contacts on the same geometry in about 13 wall-clock minutes; the margin over 0.25 covers the per-token full-vocabulary sort that n_probs > 0 forces on this build (it disables backend sampling for the slot -- server-context.cpp:1994-2004 -- and calls get_token_probabilities per generated token, server-context.cpp:2195). The added latency is not measurable offline and is a reported number of the flight, never a precondition of it. Paid API spend 0. Plan cells are RUN-CUMULATIVE across every attempt of this run id.
